title: Tackling Bias in Pre-trained Language Models: Current Trends and Under-represented Societies

bias_targets.methodology: Survey and synthesis of existing bias metrics and benchmark datasets (e.g., WinoBias, GAP, Winogender) that predominantly focus on binary gender classifications and gender-occupation associations.

Analysis of existing benchmark datasets (e.g., StereoSet, CrowS-Pairs) and an exploratory case study detailing the requirements for adapting metrics like WEAT and DisCo using New Zealand ethnicities (e.g., Māori vs. NZ European).

Evaluation of the limitations of current bias metrics and datasets when applied to under-represented societies, using New Zealand Māori as a primary case study for identifying constraints in metric-adaptation and dataset creation.
Reviewed through benchmark datasets and case studies analyzing caste and rural/urban occupation biases, particularly focusing on the Indian cultural context.
Reviewed through the categorization of bias benchmark datasets (e.g., BBQ, StereoSet) and discussed via case studies focusing on regional and religious bias representations in the Indian context.
Surveyed through benchmark datasets (e.g., WinoQueer, HolisticBias) and the review of mitigation techniques targeting LGBTQ+ stereotypes.
Surveyed via the categorization and analysis of benchmark datasets (e.g., BBQ, HolisticBias) designed to measure age-related stereotypes in language models.
Surveyed through the inclusion and analysis of benchmark datasets (e.g., BBQ, HolisticBias) that measure representational harms and stereotypes against disabled individuals.
Surveyed via the review of specific benchmark datasets (e.g., Bias NLI, UnQover) that test for biases related to national origins.
Surveyed through the analysis of benchmark datasets (e.g., BBQ, HolisticBias) that evaluate stereotypes related to body type and physical characteristics.
